phiIsNotLinear.whatIsAccountedFor: 26 is |v^perp| - 1, a FLOOR: a transvection fixes v^perp pointwise so those Paulis must conjugate with no phase. The lifts with 44 zeros have eighteen more vanishing phases than that predicts and are NOT explained here -- recorded as measured. An earlier guess that the count was uniformly 26 came from three examples and was wrong
phiIsNotLinear.linearityWouldRequire: S to preserve the Pauli cocycle, by phi(u+v) = phi(u) + phi(v) + c(Su,Sv) - c(u,v); a transvection does not, so an earlier linearity test was the wrong test

doesNotOverturnTheSplitting: d6bcf30 verified the splitting at n = 1 and the odd-p result is cited, so a homomorphic section EXISTS. What is now known is that the obvious Gauss-sum choice is not one: lifting each generator naturally and independently does not assemble into a section, which is what a nontrivial cocycle looks like even when the extension splits
